## Authors / Editors
- 李廉 (元朝) 撰

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Chūnqiū huìtōng* 春秋諸傳會通 (full title) in twenty-four juan is the *Chūnqiū* commentary of Lǐ Lián [李廉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%BB%89) of Lújiāng 廬江 — a *Zhìzhèng* 2 (1342) *jìnshì* and Xìnfēng 信豐 magistrate who died in office during the late-Yuán wars. The work is a *huìtōng* (synthesis): under each classic-passage it juxtaposes (i) the *Zuǒzhuàn* event-record, (ii) the earliest expositions of *Gōngyáng* and *Gǔliáng*, (iii) the standard commentaries of Dù Yù 杜預, Hé Xiū 何休, and Fàn Níng 范寧, (iv) the *zhèngyì* 正義 sub-commentaries, and (v) Hú Ānguó's [胡安國](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E5%AE%89%E5%9C%8B) *Chūnqiūzhuàn* ([KR1e0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0036)) as the determinative judgment, together with substantial extracts from Chén Fùliáng 陳傅良 ([KR1e0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0038)) and Zhāng Qià [張洽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%B4%BD) ([KR1e0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0048)). Lǐ's own *jǐnàn* 謹案 ("respectful note") then weighs the alternatives. The whole was completed in *Zhìzhèng* 9 / 7 (1349), thirty years after Lǐ began to study the *Chūnqiū*.

**Abstract**

The *Chūnqiū huìtōng* is the most balanced *Chūnqiū* commentary of the late Yuán: where Chéng Duānxué [程端學](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A8%8B%E7%AB%AF%E5%AD%B8) *abandons* the *zhuàn* (in the *Sānzhuàn biàn yí* [KR1e0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0062)), where Wáng Yuánjié [王元杰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%85%83%E6%9D%B0) *defers* exclusively to the Chéng-Zhū tradition (in the *Chūnqiū yàn yì* [KR1e0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0063)), and where Zhào Fǎng [趙汸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E6%B1%B8) *recovers* the *Zuǒ* against Hú Ānguó (in the cluster [KR1e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0066)–[KR1e0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0070)), Lǐ Lián takes the synthetic middle: every major commentary is given its own layer; the editor's *jǐnàn* mediates. The result is the closest the late Yuán came to a working synthesis of the *Chūnqiū* tradition, and it is not surprising that the early Qīng court-compiled *Qīndìng Chūnqiū chuánshuō huìzuǎn* ([KR1e0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0094)) drew on it heavily.

The composition date is precise: Lǐ's own preface dates the work to *Zhìzhèng* 9 / 7 / 1 (1349). The work was first circulated in copies — Lǐ's preface complains that copies were already being made before he had wished it released — and was first printed in Fēngchéng 豐城 by Jiē Gōng 揭恭, who pressed Lǐ for a preface even after the printing was complete. The bracket 1349–1349 is exact.

Methodologically the *Huìtōng* belongs to a small but important late-Sòng / Yuán type: the *zhūjiā jíyì* 諸家集議 ("collected discussions of the various masters") commentary, in which the editor's own contribution is principally the discrimination of priorities among the existing tradition rather than a fresh exegetical thesis. Lǐ states this explicitly in his *fánlì* 凡例 (general principles), reproduced after the preface: "*All the assembled commentaries here have *Zuǒ*, *Gōngyáng*, *Gǔliáng*, Hú, Chén, and Zhāng as the six masters, because all six are complete works.*" This is methodologically scrupulous — a master who is preserved only in fragments cannot be ranked with one whose whole *zhuàn* is preserved.

The cluster of mid- and late-Yuán *Chūnqiū* commentary works in this division — Chéng Duānxué's three ([KR1e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0060)–[KR1e0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0062)), Wáng Yuánjié's *Yàn yì* ([KR1e0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0063)), Lǐ Lián's *Huìtōng* (this), Zhèng Yù's *Chūnqiū quēyí* ([KR1e0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0065)), and Zhào Fǎng's five ([KR1e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0066)–[KR1e0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0070)) — collectively constitute the most concentrated period of *Chūnqiū* scholarship between the early Sòng and the late Míng.
